Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Uncontrolled (HbA1c: 9.8%) 2. Hypertension Stage II (BP at admission: 168/102 mmHg) 3. Diabetic Nephropathy - Stage 3 CKD (eGFR: 42 mL/min/1.73m²) 4. Lower Respiratory Tract Infection (LRTI) - Resolved ## CLINICAL SUMMARY Mr. Ramaiah Venkatesh, a 62-year-old male farmer from Nalgonda district, presented to the Emergency Department on 18-Oct-2024 with complaints of progressive breathlessness (Grade III), productive cough with yellow sputum, pedal oedema, and blood glucose of 380 mg/dL. He is a known diabetic and hypertensive for 8 years on irregular medication. During hospitalisation, patient was started on IV antibiotics (Injection Ceftriaxone 1g BD x 5 days), subcutaneous insulin (Actrapid sliding scale), IV Furosemide for oedema, and antihypertensives were optimised. Blood glucose was brought under control (FBS 118 mg/dL at discharge). Chest X-ray on 25-Oct showed significant clearing of bilateral infiltrates. Pedal oedema reduced to trace levels. Patient is stable at discharge. ## DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS

Avoid pickles, papad, processed foods. - Diabetic diet: Small frequent meals. Avoid rice in excess. Prefer ragi, millets. - Fluid intake: 1.5 litres/day (do NOT exceed - kidney function reduced). ## RED FLAG SYMPTOMS - RETURN TO EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY IF: - Breathlessness worsens or you cannot lie flat - Swelling of legs increases significantly - Blood sugar reading below 70 mg/dL (hypoglycaemia) - sweating, confusion - Blood pressure above 180/110 mmHg - Chest pain or palpitations ## HOME MONITORING: - Check blood sugar every morning before breakfast.
